hints: Focus on what type of gases Group 2 nitrates really produce on heating, it is not nitrogen gas.
Write the balanced equation for $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow \text{CaO} + \text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$ and balance N and O atoms.
Use the mole ratio from the balanced equation to check if 0.40 mol of reactant can really give 0.40 mol of $\text{O}_2$.
walkthrough:
**Recall the products of Group 2 nitrate decomposition**

Nitrates of Group 2 metals (except ammonium) do not give $\text{N}_2$. They give the metal oxide plus nitrogen dioxide plus oxygen.

$$2\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{CaO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Use the mole ratio to find amounts**

From the balanced equation, 2 mol of $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ gives 2 mol of $\text{CaO}$, 4 mol of $\text{NO}_2$ and 1 mol of $\text{O}_2$.

So the ratio is $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2 : \text{CaO} : \text{NO}_2 : \text{O}_2 = 2 : 2 : 4 : 1$.

**Apply to 0.40 mol and test the statements**

For 0.40 mol of $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$:
$$n(\text{CaO}) = 0.40 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{NO}_2) = 0.80 \text{ mol}$$
$$n(\text{O}_2) = 0.20 \text{ mol}$$
Statement 1 is true, statement 2 is wrong in both identity and amount, and statement 3 is wrong in amount. Only 1 is correct.

options.A: This would mean statements 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 is correct, but 2 is wrong because the nitrogen-containing product is brown $\text{NO}_2$ gas, not $\text{N}_2$. Statement 3 is also wrong because only 0.20 mol of $\text{O}_2$ forms, not 0.40 mol.
options.B: This would mean 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 1 is correct, but statement 2 claims 0.40 mol of $\text{N}_2(g)$. Thermal decomposition of $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ gives $\text{NO}_2$, with nitrogen in the +4 oxidation state, not $\text{N}_2$ where nitrogen is 0.
options.C: This would mean 2 and 3 only are correct. Both are false. No $\text{N}_2$ is formed, and the $\text{O}_2$ amount is half the claimed value because the balanced equation gives 1 mol $\text{O}_2$ from 2 mol nitrate.
options.D: This means only statement 1 is correct. 0.40 mol $\text{Ca(NO}_3)_2$ gives 0.40 mol $\text{CaO}$ in a 1:1 ratio, while the gases are 0.80 mol $\text{NO}_2$ and 0.20 mol $\text{O}_2$. So 2 and 3 are false, leaving 1 alone as true.
